predecessors.name: Mongol Empire
predecessors.text: the Jochid ulus, one of the four successor khanates of the Mongol Empire (Cliopatria row ends 1293, Golden Horde starts 1294)

successors.name: Crimean Khanate
successors.text: the Crimea and the steppe north of it, a separate state since August 1449; it sacked Sarai on 10 June 1502 and 'subjugated what remained of the Great Horde'

successors.name: Astrakhan Khanate
successors.text: the Lower Volga, 'Ahmed's descendants occupying the throne of Astrakhan in 1502'

successors.name: Nogai Horde
successors.text: the steppe east of the Volga, Edigu's Manghit ulus

capitals.name: Sarai (Old Sarai, Selitrennoye; later New Sarai)

ledger.x: 1294: the Jochid ulus appears as a separate state on Cliopatria's map when its Mongol Empire row ends in 1293.
1294: the Rus' princedoms pay tribute to Sarai.
1294: the grand principality of Vladimir is held by Sarai's appointment ('Batu installed Alexander as grand prince of Vladimir', 1252; 'Mikhail of Tver executed in Sarai', 22 November 1318).
ledger.cpn: Principality of Vladimir-Suzdal (Grand Principality of Vladimir)

ledger.x: 1294: Galicia-Volhynia is a Horde tributary.
1307: Toqta besieges Caffa.
1308: Caffa is plundered and the siege ends.
1349: Galicia-Volhynia is lost to Poland and Hungary.
1356: Jani Beg takes Tabriz.
1357: Azerbaijan is lost again.
1362: Lithuania takes Kiev and Podolia.
1362: Moldavia breaks away.
1363: the Great Troubles divide the Horde.
1363: the eastern wing, Orda's ulus, is drawn apart (Kazakh steppe, Syr Darya, Khwarazm).
1380: Tokhtamysh reunites the wings.
1381: Mamai's western horde is absorbed.
1383: Khwarazm returns to the Horde.
Spring 1387: war with Timur for Azerbaijan and the Caucasus.
1388: Timur destroys Khwarazm's tie to the Horde.
1395: the Terek decides the Caucasus.
1395: the Tokhtamysh-Timur war ends at the Terek.
1402: the eastern steppe leaves the Golden Horde on Cliopatria's map.
1405: Edigu takes Khwarazm.
1412: Khwarazm is lost.
1438: Kazan breaks away.
August 1449: Crimea throws off Sarai.
1450: the steppe east of the Volga passes to the Nogai Horde on Cliopatria's map (1,553 cells).
1453: small border losses on the Oka and Moksha.
1453: 72 cells of the same step pass to Ryazan.
1468: Astrakhan breaks away.
1480: the Ugra stand ends Moscow's vassalage.
1480: Vladimir-Suzdal (by then ruled from Moscow) leaves the vassal tint with Moscow: the Ugra stand 'formally ended the "Tatar yoke" over Russia' (Great Horde page).
ledger.cpn: Principality of Vladimir-Suzdal (Grand Principality of Vladimir)

ledger.x: June 1502: the Golden Horde ends.

wars.name: Golden Horde invasions of the Ilkhanate
wars.outcome: No border change: Oz Beg invades Azerbaijan in 1318/1319, 1324 and 1335; Abu Said dies on the way to meet the last, in Karabakh, in 1335.

wars.name: Horde-Genoese conflict at Caffa
wars.outcome: Toqta besieges Caffa in 1307 and plunders it in 1308; Jani Beg's attempt to seize it fails in 1344 and the Black Death is reported in the siege of 1346.

wars.name: Conquest of Azerbaijan by Jani Beg
wars.outcome: Tabriz is taken in 1356 and Azerbaijan is lost to Shaikh Uvais in 1357.

wars.name: Battle of Blue Waters
wars.outcome: Lithuanian victory: Kiev and a large part of present-day Ukraine pass to Lithuania, Moldavia asserts independence.

wars.name: Great Troubles
wars.outcome: Succession war after Berdi Beg's murder (August 1359); the Horde divides into Mamai's western and Orda's eastern wings until Tokhtamysh takes Sarai in 1380.

wars.name: Tokhtamysh's sack of Moscow
wars.outcome: Moscow is besieged on 23 August 1382 and stormed three days later; tribute is restored.

wars.name: Tokhtamysh-Timur war
wars.outcome: Timur routs Tokhtamysh at Kondurcha (18 June 1391) and on the Terek (15-16 April 1395) and devastates the Volga cities in the winter of 1395-96; the Golden Horde loses its southern reach.

wars.name: Battle of the Vorskla River
wars.outcome: On 12 August 1399 Edigu and Timur-Qutlugh defeat Tokhtamysh and Vytautas of Lithuania; Tokhtamysh flees to Siberia and Edigu 'united Jochi's lands under his rule' (Edigu page).

wars.name: Edigu's raid on Muscovy
wars.outcome: Edigu burns Nizhny Novgorod, Rostov and Serpukhov and besieges Moscow, which pays a ransom; no land changes.

wars.name: Break-up of the Golden Horde after Edigu
wars.outcome: After Edigu's death in 1419 the Horde 'fractured into the separate states of the Nogai Khanate, the Kazan Khanate': Kazan 1438, Crimea August 1449.

wars.name: Great Stand on the Ugra River
wars.outcome: Ahmed's campaign against Moscow of 1480; he was killed by Ibak of Sibir on 6 January 1481.

wars.name: Great Horde-Crimean Khanate war
wars.outcome: 'From 1486 to 1491, a conflict raged between the Sarai-based Great Horde and the Crimean Khanate' (Casimir IV with the Great Horde, Ivan III with Mengli I Giray); on 10 June 1502 Mengli Giray sacks Sarai and on 28 June 1502 the Great Horde ends.

certainty.note: Steppe frontiers throughout, drawn approximate; no treaty or survey line appears on the pages opened.
